title: Types of Tea
description: A collection of well-known teas with their type, origin, and caffeine level.

results.name: English Breakfast
results.notes: Full-bodied, robust blend traditionally taken with milk.

results.name: Earl Grey
results.notes: Black tea flavored with oil of bergamot, giving a citrusy aroma.

results.name: Assam
results.notes: Malty and brisk, grown in the lowlands of northeast India.

results.name: Darjeeling
results.notes: Light, floral and muscatel; called the 'champagne of teas'.

results.name: Ceylon
results.notes: Bright and citrusy black tea from the island of Sri Lanka.

results.name: Keemun
results.notes: Wine-like and slightly smoky, a classic Chinese black tea.

results.name: Lapsang Souchong
results.notes: Dried over pinewood fires for a distinctive smoky flavor.

results.name: Sencha
results.notes: Steamed green tea, grassy and refreshing; Japan's most common tea.

results.name: Matcha
results.notes: Stone-ground shade-grown leaves whisked into a frothy suspension.

results.name: Gyokuro
results.notes: Shade-grown before harvest, prized for its sweet umami character.

results.name: Dragon Well (Longjing)
results.notes: Pan-fired flat leaves with a nutty, chestnut-like taste.

results.name: Gunpowder
results.notes: Rolled into small pellets; bold and slightly smoky.

results.name: Genmaicha
results.notes: Green tea blended with roasted brown rice for a toasty flavor.

results.name: Silver Needle (Baihao Yinzhen)
results.notes: Made only from young buds; delicate, sweet and mellow.

results.name: White Peony (Bai Mudan)
results.notes: Buds and leaves; fuller and more floral than Silver Needle.

results.name: Tieguanyin
results.notes: Iron Goddess of Mercy; orchid-like and lightly oxidized.

results.name: Da Hong Pao
results.notes: Roasted rock oolong with a rich mineral, roasted character.

results.name: Dong Ding
results.notes: Traditional Taiwanese oolong, smooth with a roasted finish.

results.name: Milk Oolong (Jin Xuan)
results.notes: Naturally creamy, buttery aroma from the Jin Xuan cultivar.

results.name: Sheng Pu-erh (Raw)
results.notes: Naturally aged fermented tea; grassy young, mellowing over years.

results.name: Shou Pu-erh (Ripe)
results.notes: Pile-fermented for an earthy, smooth, dark liquor.

results.name: Chamomile
results.notes: Dried flowers with an apple-like aroma; calming before sleep.

results.name: Peppermint
results.notes: Cooling, minty infusion often used to aid digestion.

results.name: Rooibos
results.notes: Naturally sweet red bush tisane rich in antioxidants.

results.name: Hibiscus
results.notes: Tart, ruby-red infusion of dried hibiscus flowers.

results.name: Ginger
results.notes: Spicy, warming root infusion often taken for colds.
